To: the Chicago Department of Transportation (CDOT)
Subject: Request for safety study at Ashland Avenue & Cullerton Street

Dear colleagues at CDOT,

We are writing to ask you to carry out a safety study at the junction of Ashland Avenue & Cullerton Street and to consider fixes on the roads you are responsible for: South Ashland Avenue and West Cullerton Street.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 114 crashes, including 18 injury crashes. Over this period, no people were killed. The harm is valued at $1.2 million per year using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars).

No recent safety work is recorded in the official record for this junction in this period.

Based on federal evidence, we ask you to consider:

* flashing beacons at the crosswalk (Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons), expected to prevent about 0.3 pedestrian injury crashes per year, avoiding about $97,000 in harm per year.

* high-friction pavement (Pavement Friction Management), expected to prevent about 0.4 injury crashes on wet roads per year, avoiding about $129,000 in harm per year, subject to a site check for whether the pavement's friction is low now — wet-road crashes alone do not show it.

Please let us know the outcome of the study and what action you plan to take.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

cases.letter:
To: the District Department of Transportation (DDOT)
Subject: Request for safety study and signal improvements at 22nd Street NW & L Street NW

Dear colleagues at DDOT,

We are writing about the junction of 22nd Street Northwest & L Street Northwest.

The city's open record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 38 crashes including 13 injury crashes. The record of who was hurt includes 2 pedestrians injured, 3 cyclists injured, and motorists, with 0 people killed listed. In the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the yearly cost of the harm is $0.9 million. The records do not show recent safety work in this period, but list NHS - Federal Aid Pavement Restoration - NHPP Streets in 2026 as the latest recorded safety project and NHS - Federal Aid Pavement Restoration - NHPP Streets in 2027 as planned.

The site is listed as a city priority location. We respectfully ask you to carry out a safety study at this junction and, on the roads you are responsible for, to include the fixes noted below where the study shows they fit, using the plain names the city uses.

Longer yellow signal times, which would need a check that there is an entry on yellow or red and that the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice, is expected to prevent injury crashes.

Reflective backplates on the traffic signals, which would need a check for an entry on yellow or red, is expected to prevent injury crashes.

The city record shows Leading Pedestrian Interval signals are already in place. The earlier program's effect was not shown and we ask for a different approach based on the independent checks above.

Thank you for your work and consideration.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

• flashing beacons at the crosswalk (Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons, FHWA-cited, CMF 9024) — expected to prevent about 0.2 pedestrian injury crashes per year, avoiding about $65,000 in harm per year; this would pay for itself if it costs less than $0.5 million.

• better street lighting (Lighting, CMF 7774) — expected to prevent about 0.3 injury crashes in darkness per year, avoiding about $96,000 in harm per year; this would pay for itself if it costs less than $0.7 million. Please check on site whether the corner has no street lighting now, as this affects suitability.

Thank you for considering these measures.

cases.letter:
To: the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA)
Subject: Request for safety study and fixes at Turk Boulevard & Lyon Street

Dear colleagues at SFMTA,

I am writing to ask you to carry out a safety study at Turk Boulevard & Lyon Street on the roads you are responsible for: Anzavista Avenue, Encanto Avenue, Lyon Street and Turk Boulevard.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 1 crash, including 1 injury crash. No one was killed in that period.

In the U.S. DOT's official values (2024 dollars), the yearly cost of the harm recorded here is $0.1 million.

The city record does not show a recent safety project at this junction that would clearly address this harm.

Earlier at this corner there were continental crosswalks. The city's own record neither shows it worked nor rules it out, so repeating it here rests on other evidence. Please consider a different approach and test what would work best here.

Please let us know what the study finds and what action you plan on the roads under your control.

Thank you for your attention to safety at this location.

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
